title: Immune cell isolation from mouse brain and spleen for flow cytometry
author: Amandine EVEN

steps.title: Collect Brain and Spleen Tissues
steps.instruction: Prepare the mouse and collect the required tissues for isolation.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse with an intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital at 100 mg/kg.
Inject 3 µg BV711-conjugated anti-CD45 diluted in 50 µL of saline intravenously.
Allow 3 minutes for intravascular labeling prior to terminal collection and cervical dislocation.
Rapidly remove the brain and mince tissue with a scalpel.
Collect the spleen and keep it in ice-cold PBS 1X.

steps.title: Prepare Brain Cell Suspension
steps.instruction: Digest brain tissue and remove myelin to isolate cells.

substeps.instruction: Place minced brain tissue in a 15mL tube containing 4mL of collagenase D (2 mg/mL) and DNase I (28 U/mL) solution.
Incubate the tube in a 37 °C water bath for a total of 45 minutes.
Every 15 minutes, triturate with a glass pipette, transfer cells to a separate tube, and add fresh dissociation solution; repeat 3 times, reducing the pipette opening size with each repetition.
Stop enzyme activity by adding cold PBS containing 2 mM EDTA and 2% (v/v) FBS.
Pass the dissociated tissue through a 100 µm strainer to remove undigested fragments.
Centrifuge the homogenate at Room temperature for 200 x g for 2 minutes, then for 300 x g for 3 minutes, and discard the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of 37% (v/v) Percoll at Room temperature to remove myelin.
Centrifuge for 500 x g at Room temperature for 10 minutes with no brake.
Aspirate the myelin layer and wash the cell pellet with PBS-EDTA-FBS buffer.
Count recovered cells using a hemocytometer.

steps.title: Prepare Spleen Cell Suspension
steps.instruction: Dissociate spleen tissue and lyse red blood cells.

substeps.instruction: Mash the spleen tissue through a 100 µm strainer using the thumb-rest of a syringe plunger.
Rinse the filter several times with PBS-EDTA-FBS dissociation buffer to maximize recovery.
Centrifuge homogenates at 1500 rpm at 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Resuspend splenocytes in 3 mL RBC lysis buffer and incubate for 3 minutes at Room temperature.
Wash with PBS-EDTA-FBS buffer and centrifuge again for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Resuspend in 1 mL dissociation buffer, count cells, and reserve 2 million cells per spleen for staining.

steps.title: Stain and Fix Cells
steps.instruction: Perform antibody staining and cell fixation in 96-well plates at 4 °C, protected from light.

substeps.instruction: Distribute brain and spleen cells into different plates according to the experiment layout.
Centrifuge the plate at 2500 rpm at 4 °C for 40 seconds and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in fixable viability dye eFluor450 (diluted 1:1000 in 1X PBS) and incubate for 15 minutes.
Wash and centrifuge the plate at 2500 rpm at 4 °C for 40 seconds, then discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 50 µL of anti-CD16/32 Fc-blocking solution at 0.5 µg per million cells and incubate for 15 minutes.
Add 50 µL of the antibody cocktail and incubate for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge at 2500 rpm at 4 °C for 40 seconds and discard the supernatant.
Wash using PBS-EDTA-FBS buffer.
Fix cells in 100 µL of 4% PFA per well for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Acquire Flow Cytometry Data
steps.instruction: Set up controls and acquire samples using a compatible flow cytometer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare FMO controls and compensation controls using OneComp eBeads incubated with fluorescent antibodies.
Select a flow cytometer with compatible lasers and detectors (e.g., BD LSRFortessa X-20).
Acquire samples using appropriate instrument settings, such as voltages and compensation.
